title: Explain why collateral-recon on a Compute Engine VM stopped answering
telemetry: Supplied Compute Engine console views (instance details, serial port 1 output, zone operations), Cloud Monitoring Ops Agent charts, Cloud Logging gce_instance entries collected by the Ops Agent, and one sanitized clearing-gateway owner observation; the decisive packet may add a network-owner summary. The candidate has no SSH, OS Login, interactive serial console, cloud CLI or live read.
owner: Marisol, Collateral on-call, owns the investigation; Idris, the VM and application owner, owns collateral-recon-vm-01's guest OS, the collateral-recon service and its disks; Linden, the shared-network owner, owns the host project's firewall policies and network path. ITO coordinates the existing TLC and change approvals.
task: Marisol has asked for a bounded investigation after clearing-gateway reported that the collateral-recon service on Compute Engine VM collateral-recon-vm-01 stopped answering. Review the supplied console observations for 2026-10-16 09:00-09:45 UTC and return an evidence-grounded technical update for the existing TLC: what the records support about the guest and the path to it, remaining unknowns, and the next useful check with its owner. Nobody on this task has SSH or serial-console access, and no change is authorized.

sources.claim: The operating system, BIOS and other system-level entities often write to the serial ports, serial port 1 being the usual one; for a running instance the console, gcloud or REST shows only the most recent 1 MB per port. Serial port output logging to Cloud Logging is disabled by default, and sending input is the separate interactive serial console. Whether an image copies service or syslog messages to serial port 1 is image configuration, so the fixture states it as an owner note and does not grade it.

Ops Agent health is checked by querying agent.googleapis.com/agent/uptime on gce_instance for the google-cloud-ops-agent-metrics and google-cloud-ops-agent-logging components. The page reads an absent uptime metric as an agent not running properly, and names networking problems such as firewall rules, proxies or DNS when a running agent sends neither logs nor metrics, alongside missing roles, scopes or APIs. Absent agent data therefore does not by itself establish guest or application state; variant B rests on the network owner's DENIED records, not on the gap alone.

agent.googleapis.com/disk/percent_used is in the Ops Agent's default configuration, is labelled by device and by state (free, used, reserved), and is sampled every 60 seconds. The page gives no visibility delay for it, so the fixture states its own chart coverage cutoff.

During live migration the instance remains running, with a possible short period of decreased performance; migrations are reported as system events with operation type compute.instances.migrateOnHostMaintenance in the zone's operations and the System Events logs. A host error (compute.instances.hostError) crashes the instance, and an automatic restart is recorded as compute.instances.automaticRestart. The page does not quantify migration pause length; the case relies only on the migration completing with the VM running.

When a firewall policy rule with logging enabled applies to a VM's traffic, Cloud Logging records the connection; disposition is ALLOWED, DENIED or INTERCEPTED, and a hierarchical policy rule reference has the form {folder tier index}/firewallPolicy:{id}. The NET-4471 record is a supplied network-owner summary; the case does not rely on the log name or monitored resource of these records.

gce_instance (VM Instance) identifies a Compute Engine VM with project_id, instance_id (the numeric identifier) and zone labels. The fixture's syslog and app.log entries are labelled supplied records attributed to that resource, not native exports.

a.conclusion: Inside the guest, collateral-recon exited after spool writes to the full /srv/collateral data disk failed, and systemd stopped restarting it at 09:13:33Z; that matches clearing-gateway's failed connections and the last app.log line. The Ops Agent kept reporting throughout, so the guest stayed observable, and the network owner reports no change or denied connections. The 08:47 live migration completed with the VM running and is not linked to the failure. What filled the data disk, and whether spooled batches are complete, is unproven.
next_checks: Idris, the VM and application owner, identifies what grew /srv/collateral from 06:00Z (spool, retained batches or another writer) and the state of the 09:12 batch, using the owner's existing authorized access.

Idris proposes, under ITO's change approval in the existing TLC, how to free or extend space and when to restart collateral-recon; a disk resize is a mitigation for the owner to propose, not an authorized or cause fix.

Marisol watches sdb disk utilization, collateral-recon syslog entries and clearing-gateway handoffs after the 09:40 sample, and confirms with clearing-gateway's owner which batches need reprocessing before any replay.

Assuming SSH, OS Login or interactive serial-console access, or claiming to have inspected the guest directly.
Resizing the disk, deleting spool files or restarting the service as an authorized step or a demonstrated cause fix.
Declaring recovery from RUNNING status or from the continuing agent metrics.
unknowns: What wrote to /srv/collateral from 06:00Z and whether it is still writing.
Whether the 09:12 batch and earlier spool files are complete, and which clearing handoffs need reprocessing.
The state of the service and disk after the 09:42 capture.

b.conclusion: The guest's telemetry and the service's ingress path stopped together at about 09:12, when rules in firewall policy change NET-4471 began denying the VM's egress to Google API endpoints and clearing-gateway's ingress on TCP 8443. The VM reports RUNNING and the last guest observations matched the previous day, but there is no guest observation after 09:12:39Z, so collateral-recon's own state is unknown rather than failed. The 08:47 live migration completed earlier with the VM running and is not linked.
next_checks: Linden, the shared-network owner, confirms whether NET-4471's rules were meant to match collateral-recon's subnet and decides, under ITO's change approval, whether to revert or narrow them.
Once the path is restored, Idris and Marisol read Ops Agent uptime, syslog and app.log for the gap and confirm collateral-recon's state before anyone restarts or changes the VM.
Marisol keeps clearing-gateway's owner informed in the existing TLC and confirms which handoffs need reprocessing after the service answers again; no replay before that check.
unsupported: Diagnosing a full disk, a crashed service or another guest fault from the absent agent data or the stopped application log.
Resetting, stopping or restarting the VM or service, resizing a disk, or assuming SSH or serial-console access to look inside the guest.
Blaming the 08:47 live migration, or treating RUNNING status as proof that collateral-recon is healthy.
Presenting a firewall change as authorized by this investigation or as already confirmed to be unintended.
unknowns: Whether collateral-recon is still running and whether a batch was in flight at 09:12.
Whether NET-4471 was intended to cover this subnet and which other workloads it affects.
The state of the VM, service and path after the 09:42 capture.
